example.romaji: kesa no shinbun yonda?
example.ja: 今朝の新聞読んだ？
example.english: Did you read this morning's paper?

examplePolite.romaji: kesa no shinbun yomimashita ka?
examplePolite.ja: 今朝の新聞読みましたか？
examplePolite.english: Did you read this morning's paper?

notes: Goes with yomu (read); shinbun o toru means to subscribe.

use: In daily talk it mostly means calm, nothing going on.

example.romaji: kyou wa nanimo nakute heiwa da ne.
example.ja: 今日は何もなくて平和だね。
example.english: Nothing's going on today, it's nice and peaceful.

examplePolite.romaji: kyou wa nanimo nakute heiwa desu ne.
examplePolite.ja: 今日は何もなくて平和ですね。
examplePolite.english: Nothing's going on today, it's nice and peaceful.

notes: Also the noun peace, as in sekai heiwa (world peace).

use: Mostly heard in kojinteki ni (personally, for me) and kojin jouhou (personal data).

example.romaji: kojinteki ni wa kotchi no hou ga suki.
example.ja: 個人的にはこっちのほうが好き。
example.english: Personally, I like this one better.

examplePolite.romaji: kojinteki ni wa kotchi no hou ga suki desu.
examplePolite.ja: 個人的にはこっちのほうが好きです。
examplePolite.english: Personally, I like this one better.

notes: For your private life, say puraibeeto, not kojin.

use: Sounds serious, like an alarm or the news; for an everyday rush people often say isogi.

example.romaji: kinkyuu no youji ga dekita kara, saki ni kaeru ne.
example.ja: 緊急の用事ができたから、先に帰るね。
example.english: Something urgent came up, so I'm heading home first.

examplePolite.romaji: kinkyuu no youji ga dekita node, saki ni kaerimasu.
examplePolite.ja: 緊急の用事ができたので、先に帰ります。
examplePolite.english: Something urgent came up, so I'll head home first.

notes: Kinkyuu jishin sokuhou is the earthquake alert that blares on phones.

use: The forms and steps for official things: moving, banks, visas, cancelling.

example.romaji: kuyakusho de tetsuzuki shinakya.
example.ja: 区役所で手続きしなきゃ。
example.english: I have to do the paperwork at the ward office.

examplePolite.romaji: kuyakusho de tetsuzuki o shinai to ikenai n desu.
examplePolite.ja: 区役所で手続きをしないといけないんです。
examplePolite.english: I have to do the paperwork at the ward office.

notes: Goes with suru (tetsuzuki suru) and often with mendoukusai (a pain).

example.romaji: sore, zettai sagi da yo.
example.ja: それ、絶対詐欺だよ。
example.english: That's definitely a scam.

examplePolite.romaji: sore wa zettai sagi desu yo.
examplePolite.ja: それは絶対詐欺ですよ。
examplePolite.english: That's definitely a scam.

notes: Casually also for anything misleading: shashin sagi is a photo far better than the real thing.

example.romaji: shuumatsu, kanojo to deeto suru n da.
example.ja: 週末、彼女とデートするんだ。
example.english: I've got a date with my girlfriend this weekend.

examplePolite.romaji: shuumatsu, kanojo to deeto suru n desu.
examplePolite.ja: 週末、彼女とデートするんです。
examplePolite.english: I've got a date with my girlfriend this weekend.

notes: Used as deeto suru or deeto ni iku. Never a calendar date; that's hizuke.

use: Anything you carry or have delivered.

example.romaji: omoi desho, nimotsu motsu yo.
example.ja: 重いでしょ、荷物持つよ。
example.english: That's heavy, right? I'll take your bags.

examplePolite.romaji: omoi deshou, nimotsu mochimashou ka?
examplePolite.ja: 重いでしょう、荷物持ちましょうか？
examplePolite.english: That looks heavy. Shall I carry your bags?

notes: A delivery is also nimotsu: nimotsu ga todoita (a parcel came).

use: Kaeri ni = on the way home.

example.romaji: kaeri ni konbini yotte kuru ne.
example.ja: 帰りにコンビニ寄ってくるね。
example.english: I'll stop at the convenience store on the way home.

examplePolite.romaji: kaeri ni konbini ni yotte kimasu.
examplePolite.ja: 帰りにコンビニに寄ってきます。
examplePolite.english: I'll stop at the convenience store on the way home.

notes: Kaeri wa nanji? asks what time someone will be back. The verb is kaeru.

use: Covers both the party and the gift or money you give.

example.romaji: tanjoubi no oiwai shiyou yo.
example.ja: 誕生日のお祝いしようよ。
example.english: Let's celebrate your birthday.

examplePolite.romaji: tanjoubi no oiwai o shimashou.
examplePolite.ja: 誕生日のお祝いをしましょう。
examplePolite.english: Let's celebrate your birthday.

notes: Oiwai suru = to celebrate. What you actually say to the person is omedetou.

use: A cocktail-style bar; a cheap place for drinks and food is an izakaya.

example.romaji: kono ato, baa de ippai nomanai?
example.ja: この後、バーで一杯飲まない？
example.english: Want to grab a drink at a bar after this?

examplePolite.romaji: kono ato, baa de ippai nomimasen ka?
examplePolite.ja: この後、バーで一杯飲みませんか？
examplePolite.english: Would you like a drink at a bar after this?

example.romaji: natsuyasumi, dokoka ryokou ikanai?
example.ja: 夏休み、どこか旅行行かない？
example.english: Want to go on a trip somewhere over the summer break?

examplePolite.romaji: natsuyasumi ni dokoka ryokou ni ikimasen ka?
examplePolite.ja: 夏休みにどこか旅行に行きませんか？
examplePolite.english: Would you like to take a trip somewhere over the summer break?

notes: Goes with iku: ryokou ni iku. A business trip is shutchou, not ryokou.

use: For restaurants, hotels, doctors, haircuts; the noun yoyaku is the booking itself.

example.romaji: mise, shichiji ni yoyaku shitoita yo.
example.ja: 店、7時に予約しといたよ。
example.english: I booked the restaurant for seven.

examplePolite.romaji: omise, shichiji ni yoyaku shite okimashita.
examplePolite.ja: お店、7時に予約しておきました。
examplePolite.english: I've booked the restaurant for seven.

notes: On arrival you say yoyaku shita tanaka desu (I'm Tanaka, I have a booking).

use: A planned party; drinks with friends or coworkers is usually a nomikai.

example.romaji: kin'you, tomodachi no ie de paatii aru n da.
example.ja: 金曜、友達の家でパーティーあるんだ。
example.english: There's a party at a friend's place on Friday.

examplePolite.romaji: kin'youbi ni tomodachi no ie de paatii ga aru n desu.
examplePolite.ja: 金曜日に友達の家でパーティーがあるんです。
examplePolite.english: There's a party at a friend's place on Friday.

notes: Common as tanjoubi paatii (birthday party) and hoomu paatii (party at someone's home).

example.romaji: mou osoi shi, takushii de kaerou.
example.ja: もう遅いし、タクシーで帰ろう。
example.english: It's late, let's take a taxi home.

examplePolite.romaji: mou osoi node, takushii de kaerimashou.
examplePolite.ja: もう遅いので、タクシーで帰りましょう。
examplePolite.english: It's late, so let's take a taxi home.

notes: Goes with noru (ride) and yobu (call): takushii o yobu.

example.romaji: raigetsu, tomodachi no kekkonshiki ni iku n da.
example.ja: 来月、友達の結婚式に行くんだ。
example.english: I'm going to a friend's wedding next month.

examplePolite.romaji: raigetsu, tomodachi no kekkonshiki ni ikimasu.
examplePolite.ja: 来月、友達の結婚式に行きます。
examplePolite.english: I'm going to a friend's wedding next month.

notes: Kekkon alone is marriage; -shiki makes it the ceremony. Guests give cash, called goshuugi.

english: souvenir; gift brought back from a trip
use: Usually snacks brought back for family, friends or coworkers, or a small gift when visiting.

example.romaji: kore, kyouto no omiyage. minna de tabete.
example.ja: これ、京都のお土産。みんなで食べて。
example.english: This is from Kyoto. Share it with everyone.

examplePolite.romaji: kore, kyouto no omiyage desu. minasan de douzo.
examplePolite.ja: これ、京都のお土産です。皆さんでどうぞ。
examplePolite.english: This is from Kyoto. Please share it, everyone.

use: The everyday word for trains, including the subway.

example.romaji: densha okureteru kara, chotto okureru.
example.ja: 電車遅れてるから、ちょっと遅れる。
example.english: The train's delayed, so I'll be a bit late.

examplePolite.romaji: densha ga okurete iru node, sukoshi okuremasu.
examplePolite.ja: 電車が遅れているので、少し遅れます。
examplePolite.english: The train is delayed, so I'll be a little late.

notes: Get on is densha ni noru, get off is oriru. The bullet train is shinkansen.

use: Concerts, fan meetups, festivals, in-store promotions.

example.romaji: kondo no doyoubi, ibento ikanai?
example.ja: 今度の土曜日、イベント行かない？
example.english: Want to go to an event this Saturday?

examplePolite.romaji: kondo no doyoubi, ibento ni ikimasen ka?
examplePolite.ja: 今度の土曜日、イベントに行きませんか？
examplePolite.english: Would you like to go to an event this Saturday?

example.romaji: eki made basu de ikou ka.
example.ja: 駅までバスで行こうか。
example.english: Shall we take the bus to the station?

examplePolite.romaji: eki made basu de ikimashou ka.
examplePolite.ja: 駅までバスで行きましょうか。
examplePolite.english: Shall we take the bus to the station?

notes: Basu also means bath in loanwords like basutaoru (bath towel); a bath itself is ofuro.
